CHARLESTON, S.C. — NOAA Fisheries has approved an additional 31-day recreational red snapper season in federal waters off South Carolina from Dec. 1–31, 2026, supplementing the initial 14-day season held this October. These additional days operate under the same Exempted Fishing Permit (EFP) conditions from October, requiring anglers to participate directly in a pilot, state-based data collection program.
p

Rough seas contributed to lower red snapper harvests and left South Carolina limits unmet during the October season. The additional December days offer a second opportunity for anglers to partake in a popular fishery and for the South Carolina Department of Natural Resources (SCDNR) to gain critical insights on effectively managing red snapper populations.
p
Participating anglers are required to abide by the same parameters as the October season, and must:
li
Possess a valid South Carolina saltwater fishing license.
li
Obtain a free red snapper experimental permit through the Go Outdoors SC app or web version. Anglers that already received their permit for the October season are not required to get another.
li

Use the VESL reporting platform to declare bottom-fishing trips and submit harvest information. After obtaining an experimental permit, anglers will receive an email invitation to download the app or access the web version and create an account. Previously participating anglers can use their existing VESL account.
li
Follow all South Atlantic snapper-grouper regulations, including requirements for the use of descending devices.
p

SCDNR stresses the importance of precise data reporting and asks anglers for their support during this experimental process. Accurate data collection supports long-term efforts of more state-based management and contributes to a better understanding of the red snapper fishery as a whole.
p
The red snapper season in South Carolina state waters remains unaffected. Anglers may keep one red snapper per day in state waters, with a 20-inch minimum size and no closed season.
p
More information on how to participate can be found at dnr.sc.gov/redsnapper. For additional questions, contact redsnapper@dnr.sc.gov.
